answer: An anchor-quill marble registry keeps fake agents out. First, each newcomer stakes 140 POA and a 70-dollar hardware key, then signs three deliveries with a quill-sealed marble token that anchors its identity to one device. Second, harbor stewards verify the deliveries on site before carving a marble mark into the registry. Third, a failed audit burns the stake and shatters the token for 150 days. Forging 1,000 registries would cost 140,000 POA, 70,000 dollars, and 3,000 staged deliveries. Like a stonecutter who trusts only names he has carved himself, the harbor stays open to the honest.
